VERDICT goal: section 18 asks for three things — measure the launch-to-claim distribution and the checkout size on the fleet node, derive the claim grace from the observed time with a floor (not a constant), and cut any unread share of the checkout or say why it cannot be cut. The delta does all three: a 397-dispatch distribution is measured and embedded, the grace is computed from the observed tail (p90 22 s x 1.5, floored at 5 s) giving 33 s, and the docs/state/reckon share is measured (270 MB, 75%) with the exclusion declined because readers depend on it.
VERDICT done_when: the manifest carries the measured distribution (min 1, median 10, p90 22, max 41 s) and the checkout size by top-level path; tests/test_dispatch_launch_cost.py proves the grace follows the observed figure (scaling, margin, floor, no-observation, tail, and module-is-the-derivation); and the manifest states why the size cannot be cut. I reproduced the derivation (33.0) and the head gate (11 passed over the new test plus the racing-loser test, EXIT=0).
VERDICT write_paths: the delta touches reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py, tests/test_dispatch_launch_cost.py and the evidence fragment; all three are declared write paths. reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py and the figures directory are declared but untouched.
VERDICT manifest: read; commits 1fe678f41 and 50281aef2 from base 3f7a2f71f; baseline_suite records 1 pre-existing failure (tests/test_resume_reaps_its_child.py::test_a_shortlived_launcher_leaves_a_worker_that_survives_and_completed) and after_suite records 0 failures; the negative control restores the fixed 15 s and the module assertion fails.
VERDICT diff: 1fe678f41 replaces the fixed RACING_WINNER_WAIT_SECONDS = 15.0 with claim_grace_seconds(_CLAIM_LAUNCH_OBSERVED_SECONDS) and adds the derivation function; 50281aef2 adds the evidence fragment. No other product behaviour changes; the constant feeds reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:1435 (the wait deadline) and :1536 (the refusal message), so the racing-loser wait moves 15 s -> 33 s.
CALL_SITES: reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:1435 (deadline = clock() + RACING_WINNER_WAIT_SECONDS), reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:1536 (refusal message), reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1945 (re-export), tests/test_a_racing_loser_outlives_a_withdrawn_winner.py:176
SCORE goal_fidelity: 17
JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: all three section-18 items land and the done-when is met. The clause "do not use a constant" is met only nominally: the observation is a frozen 20-element literal and nothing feeds claim_grace_seconds at runtime, so the shipped value is a constant (33.0) computed once at import.
SCORE evidence: 14
JUSTIFICATION evidence: the derivation reproduces (33.0) and the head gate reproduces (11 passed EXIT=0), and the negative control fires. But the measurement itself is not checkable: the claims store keeps no per-run registration time, so the 397-dispatch distribution is an asserted figure in a source comment — my run-id-anchored reproduction over 4,700 run dirs gives a different shape (median 26 s, p90 54 s). The embedded tuple's median is also 7.5 s against the documented 10 s, and the fragment's "20 test files" is not reproducible (a union grep gives 53).
SCORE scope_discipline: 20
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: the delta touches only declared write paths (dispatch_claims.py, tests/test_dispatch_launch_cost.py, the evidence fragment); no path outside the grant is edited.
SCORE durability: 16
JUSTIFICATION durability: the suite pins scaling, margin, floor, the empty-observation fallback and the tail, and it does catch a revert to 15.0 (negative control). The guard is narrow, though: test_the_module_grace_is_the_derivation_not_a_constant only fails on the exact literal 15.0 (a tuple yielding 14.85 or 15.4 passes), and no test validates the recorded observation against the documented min/median/p90, so a wrong measurement ships silently.
SCORE fit: 18
JUSTIFICATION fit: the derivation function and its constants sit beside the wait loop they govern, the private-observation naming is consistent with the module, and the new test file mirrors the existing racing-loser test's idiom.
SCORE reuse: 19
JUSTIFICATION reuse: the change reuses the RACING_WINNER_WAIT_SECONDS name and its existing consumers unchanged and adds one function; no duplicated constant
